claim: Computers span tiny accessories through thin book-sized devices.
originalWording: Computers span tiny accessories through thin book-sized devices.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 4, printed pp. 13–14

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Computers are sold in a wide range of small personal forms, including tiny accessories and thin book-sized devices.
reference.rationale: Clip-on shuffle, smartphones, Kindle and thin laptops are concrete pre-deadline form factors. Illustrative rings/earrings need not all become equally popular for the varied-miniaturization claim to succeed.

evidence.title: Apple: Small clip-on iPod shuffle
evidence.note: Primary institutional, research, or issuer source. Dates in the claim refer to the observation or product event, not the review date.. Primary institutional, research, or issuer source. Dates in the claim refer to the observation or product event, not the review date.

evidence.title: Apple introduces MacBook Air
evidence.note: Opening notebook description and hardware/features paragraphs. The announcement documents an unusually thin notebook and built-in wireless features. Evidence limits: It is one full-sized notebook, not evidence for the full range of tiny computing form factors.

evidence.title: Introducing Amazon Kindle
evidence.note: Opening product description and Holds Hundreds of Books in 10.3 Ounces section. The 2007 Kindle is a small electronic-reading form factor with wireless access and local storage. Evidence limits: Its listed functions and size do not make it a general-purpose keyboard-free computer.

evidence.title: iPhone App Store downloads top 10 million
evidence.note: Opening iPhone/iPod touch description and native-application availability paragraph. The release documents a programmable mobile-device application ecosystem before 2009. Evidence limits: This citation establishes available applications, not physical dimensions or every proposed form factor.

evidence.title: Apple introduces iPod shuffle (2005)
evidence.note: Opening wearable-device description and USB flash-drive paragraph. The shipping player demonstrates a small wearable digital device with flash storage and computer connectivity. Evidence limits: A music player is not a substitute for every general-purpose-computer form factor in the forecast.

evidence.title: Apple reinvents the phone with iPhone
evidence.note: Opening product description and Pricing & Availability section. The 2007 announcement describes a small handheld combining phone, media player and Internet functions. Evidence limits: The source documents a planned product and functions, not universality or the success of every miniature form factor.
